title: Zoom Workflow: How to Set Up Automation (2026 Guide)
summary: Zoom Workflow is Zoom's no-code automation tool. It connects one trigger to one action inside your account, separate from meeting settings or external…
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Only if the first branch runs does a second one help, and these five questions are where first runs most often stall. The body doesn't settle them, so each answer points to the Zoom documentation that does.


Is Zoom Workflow free? Partly. Availability and run allowances depend on your Zoom plan, and the Free tier is capped. One question stays open: whether test runs count against the Free quota.


Treat them as if they do until Zoom's plan documentation says otherwise, or you may spend your allowance before the real trigger ever fires. Check Zoom's pricing and plan-comparison pages.


### Can Zoom Workflow start from a webhook or a schedule?


Before you assume a webhook or timer exists, open the trigger picker and read what is listed. Which trigger types you get depends on what the workflow builder offers for your plan and account.


If the trigger you need is missing, Zoom's Workflow documentation is the place to confirm whether it is unsupported or gated by plan. Don't build a branch around a trigger you haven't seen fire in a test.


Why didn't my Zoom workflow run after a meeting ended? The usual cause is a permission, a connection scope or a plan limit, not the workflow logic. Work through them in this order:


1. Confirm the workflow is published and switched on.
2. Confirm the account that owns the connection can see that meeting.
3. Confirm the connection was granted the scope the action needs.
4. Confirm you haven't exhausted your run allowance.
5. Check that the event you chose matches what you wanted. "Meeting ended" and "recording available" are separate events, and the second can arrive well after the first.


Where your plan exposes it, run history is the first place to look. A silent failure there is more useful than no record at all.


### Can I use Zoom Workflow without being an admin?


Sometimes, and the limit is usually the connection, not the builder. Whether a non-admin can create workflows, authorize connections, or install account-level apps is controlled by account settings, so an admin may have to enable it.


If a colleague's workflow works and yours doesn't, compare roles before comparing steps. Zoom's admin and role-permission documentation covers who can do what.


### How is Zoom Workflow different from Zoom Marketplace apps?


For chaining a trigger to actions inside your account, Workflow is the builder.


Install and authorize a Marketplace app and it brings its own scopes and approval rules, because these are separate integrations.


A workflow may rely on a connection to an app, so a failure can sit in either place. Zoom's Marketplace documentation covers app installation and permissions; its Workflow documentation covers the builder.
